match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the natural, labour and capital classification together with how cost, availability and quality decide which resource a business uses; the closest, the Economics scarcity card, covers factors of production in a broader economic setting, and the start-up resources card lists different resources.

draft.title: Business resources
card: Natural
things taken from the earth, such as land, water, timber and minerals. A farm or a mine depends on them.
Labour
the physical and mental work of people, including their skills and knowledge. A business hires staff to supply it.
Capital
made items used to produce goods or services, such as machinery, tools, vehicles and buildings. Money used to buy them is not itself this resource.
A business weighs the cost, availability and quality of each resource when it decides which to use and how much.
draft.remember: Natural comes from the earth, labour is people's work, and capital is made items used to produce. Cost, availability and quality guide the choice.

a.q: Priya's bakery in Ballarat buys a new commercial oven. Which resource is the oven?
opts: Capital, because it is a made item used to produce bread
Natural, because it is made from metal taken from the earth
Labour, because it does the work that a baker would do
Natural, because it uses gas or electricity to run
a.why: The oven was made by people and is used to produce bread, so it is capital. The metal in it began as a natural resource, but the finished oven is a made item. It does not supply human work, so it is not labour.
a.clue: Was it made by people to help produce goods?

b.q: Tom runs a joinery in Geelong. Skilled carpenters are scarce and costly, so he buys a machine that cuts timber panels. Which factor most directly led to this choice?
opts: The availability and cost of labour
The quality of the natural resource
The low cost of capital resources
The availability of natural resources
b.why: Skilled carpenters are scarce and costly, so the cost and availability of labour pushed Tom towards capital. Timber is a natural resource, but nothing in the case says it is hard to get or poor in quality.
b.clue: Look at which resource Tom found scarce and costly.

a.best: Capital, because it is a made item used to produce bread

b.best: The availability and cost of labour

b.q: Tom's joinery in Geelong has advertised for carpenters for six months with no applicants, and the few nearby ask for high wages. He buys a panel-cutting machine instead. What best explains his choice?
opts: Labour was low in availability and high in cost
Capital was low in availability and high in cost
Natural resources were low in quality and high in cost
Labour was high in quality and low in cost
b.why: No applicants means labour is hard to get, and high wages mean it is costly, so Tom swapped some labour for capital. Capital cannot be the scarce resource, because he was able to buy the machine. Nothing in the case says the timber was poor.
b.clue: Which resource is Tom using less of after the change?
